newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 20.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

The government has agreed to publish an interim report by Sir Gordon Downey, Parliament's Commissioner for Standards, after the Labour Party accused the Tories of delaying its publication because of the general election. A leak to The Times newspaper revealed that former Tory minister Tim Smith and senior Tory backbencher Sir Michael Grylls received more money from lobbyist Ian Greer than was disclosed to the Privileges Committee.
CITY TO EARN 120 MLN STG FROM NORWICH FLOAT

Insurance group Norwich Union has announced a five billion stg stock market flotation. Underwriters and City advisers are set to earn over 120 million stg in fees. Chief executive Allan Brigewater said that no directors have been given share option contracts at present. Policyholders will receive a 1,000 stg windfall if more than three-quarters of them accept the plan.
POUND FORCES BIG NEW BRITISH STEEL JOB CUTS

British Steel has refused to confirm reports that between 5,000 and 10,000 jobs, including management positions, could be axed over the next five years. The strength of the pound and strong competition, highlighted by Krupp Hoesch's bid for rival Thyssen in Germany, has been blamed by industry analysts.
